correctness.rationale: Menon--Singh's path-concatenation operation can be iterated until any nonpath tree is coefficientwise dominated by a three-arm spider. I independently checked the arm-state generating function and the resulting low coefficients z(S(a,b,c);2)=9-2t and, when all arms have length at least two, z(S(a,b,c);3)=13n-66+2r. The high-coefficient obstruction also checks: the four vertices on the two length-two arms form a fort in A_n=S(2,2,n-5), so z(A_n;n-4)<C(n,4); in B_n=S(2,4,n-7), n>=11, a fort omitting the center needs at least 2+3=5 vertices across two arms, while a fort containing the center needs at least 1+1+2+2=6 vertices, so there is no fort of size at most four and z(B_n;n-4)=C(n,4). These comparisons exhaust the dominated spider cases and prove that no nonpath tree is greatest. Independent small-order brute-force checks of the spider formulas agree with the record.

originality.rationale: The record disclosed Li--Cao--Ji (2025), DOI 10.1007/s00373-025-02925-6, as a potentially covering inaccessible source. I first checked open-access/search sources and then used authorized Oxford institutional retrieval; the complete 10-page article is about the minimum zero forcing number F(T), connected forcing number F_c(T), total forcing number F_t(T), and differences/equality cases among those parameters. It does not treat zero-forcing polynomial coefficients or a coefficientwise runner-up/coatom theorem. Menon--Singh supplies the monotone path-concatenation transformation, Boyer et al. supplies the known two-vertex spider count, and fort papers supply background; none of the inspected statements gives the present incompatibility theorem. Priority remains qualified against unindexed work.

scientific_value.rationale: The theorem gives an infinite-family structural obstruction to a universal second-best tree, with two explicit witnesses and only three coefficient positions needed to defeat every candidate. It identifies a genuine tradeoff between small forcing sets and small fort obstructions and yields at least two coatoms in the tree polynomial poset, while correctly stopping short of classifying all coatoms.

citations.note: K. Menon and A. Singh, Exploring the influence of graph operations on zero forcing sets; source of the coefficientwise path-concatenation operation used in the reduction.
K. Boyer et al., The zero forcing polynomial of a graph; source for established low-coefficient spider/path facts.

B. Li, Y. Cao and S. Ji, The Extremal Results for Forcing Problem of Trees. Complete 10-page full text obtained through authorized Oxford access after OA attempts failed; it concerns minimum/connected/total forcing numbers, not zero-forcing polynomial coefficient extrema.
Becker et al., On the number of minimal forts of a graph; prior fort structure/counting context.

limitations: The theorem proves nonexistence of a greatest nonpath tree for n>=11 but does not classify all maximal elements or prove threshold 11 optimal.
The originality conclusion is based on inspected named sources plus targeted searches; it is not an exhaustive guarantee against unindexed contemporaneous work.
